overview.title: Index: B to C (backbone to Conv3D)
overview.central_idea: This page covers all of B and the start of C: backpropagation, batch normalization, binary and categorical classification, bidirectional RNNs, callbacks, class activation maps, CNNs and the Conv layers.
overview.importance: Use it to find the core mechanics (backpropagation, the chain rule, computation graphs) and the main classification chapters.

summary:
Index page printed 610 (PDF 634). It covers **B** (backbone to byte-pair encoding) and the start of **C** (C4 to Conv3D layer). Locators are **printed** pages: **add 24** for the PDF page.

**Major clusters**
- **How training works.** *backpropagation* 63, with *algorithm* 9, 46–50 (PDF 33, 70–74). *chain rule* 46 (PDF 70). *computation graphs* 47–50 (PDF 71–74). *continuous function* 41.
- **Normalization.** *batch normalization* 276–278 (PDF 300–302). *BatchNormalization layer* 216, 265, 445, 603.
- **Classification.** *classification* 104, 352 (PDF 128), with sub-entries movie reviews 106–116 (PDF 130–140), multiclass classification 116–126 (PDF 140–150) and regression 126–134. *binary classification* 105, 110, 601. *categorical_crossentropy* 119, 126, 601. *classification and regression, glossary* 105 (PDF 129).
- **Text and sequences.** *bag-of-words model* 399–402 (PDF 423–426). *bigram model* 403–404. *byte-pair encoding* 391 (PDF 415). *character tokenization* 387–390. *CBOW* 462. *BERT* 455 (PDF 479). *causal language model* 455. *bidirectional* RNNs 377–378 (PDF 401–402).
- **Vision.** *CNNs* 231–241, 602 (PDF 255–265). *class activation heatmaps* 299–306 (PDF 323–330). *COCO dataset* 332. *Conv1D/Conv2D/Conv3D* layers. *Conv2DTranspose* 316, 347. *backbone* 257, 258, 336.
- **Keras workflow.** *callbacks* 208 (PDF 232). *compile()* 191, 425. *build()* 193, 541. *call()* 215, 475. *compute_loss()* 516, 526. *best practices* 538–556.
- **Big-picture ideas.** *broad generalization* 576, *cognitive automation vs. cognitive autonomy* 13, *compositional generalization* 593, *concept drift* 177, 188.

concepts.name: backpropagation (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 63, with 'algorithm 9, 46–50' (PDF 33, 70–74). The chain rule is at 46 (PDF 70) and computation graphs at 47–50 (PDF 71–74).
concepts.intuition: PDF 33 gives the first intuitive picture. PDF 70–74 work through the algorithm on a computation graph.
concepts.technical: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to a computation graph to get the gradient of the loss with respect to each weight.
concepts.significance: Every training loop in the book depends on it.
concepts.example: To review the chain rule, open PDF 70.
concepts.misconception: Printed 46 is not PDF 46. It is PDF 70.

concepts.name: batch normalization (index entry)
concepts.definition: batch normalization is at printed 276–278 (PDF 300–302). The BatchNormalization layer is at 216, 265, 445, 603.
concepts.intuition: The full explanation is in the ConvNet architecture-patterns section. The other locators show the layer being used.
concepts.technical: Printed 216 (PDF 240) relates to non-trainable weights in custom training. Printed 603 is the conclusions review.
concepts.significance: It is a key architecture pattern for deep ConvNets.
concepts.misconception: The pages that only use the layer do not all explain it again.
